idiom_name: is-test with smart cast against per-element visitor interfaces
implementation_notes: Kotlin keeps the role structure and simplifies the test: one interface per element extending an empty marker interface, and an accept whose body is if (visitor is CircleVisitor) visitor.visit(this) - the smart cast removes the explicit cast that Java still needs, and the else branch is the visitor that cannot visit this element. What the language offers instead is a sealed hierarchy plus a when expression, which the Kotlin documentation recommends because the compiler then proves coverage, but a sealed hierarchy is closed and therefore answers the closed-set row rather than this one. Keep the interface-per-element visitor when element types are added by other modules or shipped as plugins.
pitfalls: is on an interface is a runtime test that any implementation passes, so keep element interfaces single-method and narrowly named or unrelated visitables start matching.

Smart casts cannot be relied on for properties with custom getters or mutable vals, where the compiler must assume the value may change - the visit call then needs an explicit as and an unchecked-cast warning appears.

Sealed interfaces close the hierarchy, so using when without an else is exhaustive only because the element set is closed, which contradicts the reason for choosing the acyclic pattern in the first place.
